newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian petrol pump attendants scale down strike.
newsitem.headline: Italian petrol pump attendants scale down strike.

text.p: Petrol pump attendants in Italy said on Friday that they would cut a planned three-day strike next week to 24 hours in a sign of goodwill.
The decision to limit the stoppage to one day, from 1700 GMT on Tuesday to 1700 GMT on Wednesday, followed talks between their organisation and Industry Minister Pierluigi Bersani.
Bersani said the ministry had agreed to organise talks on a restructuring of the sector and welcomed the group's decision to limit their stoppage.
The attendants are angry over reductions in petrol prices in Italy, where virtually all fuel stations are manned.
The main state-owned oil company ENI has announced discounts for motorists who fill their own tanks but wants service stations to cover part of the discount.
Friday's decision by the pump attendants was welcome news for Italians, who are being plagued by a string of strikes in the transport sector.
Air traffic controllers stopped work this week and plan further action in Milan on April 18.
A wildcat bus drivers' strike in Rome on Tuesday brought the city to a standstill as commuters struggled to reach work.
A four-day sea transport strike was due to start on April 19. Railway workers have called a 24-hour stoppage on the same day.
